title: First Year Seminar
description: Music 100 is a first semester colloquium course for music majors. Music 100 provides insight into the various career tracks in the musical field. This course will also introduce music students to the many campus resources available to them throughout their time at SDSU.
notes: This course is for first year music students.

title: Recitals
description: Preparation for individual solo performances and attendance at a minimum of 12 concerts or recitals in accordance with music requirements.

title: Music for Elementary Classroom Teachers
description: Rudimentary music theory involving the elements of music: melody, rhythm, and harmony. Developing the understanding of these elements through instrumental and vocal experiences which include the use of unison and part-singing, the keyboard, and simple melodic and harmonic instruments. For liberal studies and preservice teachers.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Introduction to Elements of Music
description: Music from aesthetic, communicative, theoretical, and creative perspective. Development of understanding of aesthetic valuing, musical notation, rhythm, theory, pitch, aural skills, and musical terminology.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Aural Musicianship II

title: Introduction to Music Studies
description: Introduction to the study of music in academia, including a survey of professional opportunities and the development of applied skills in critical thinking, listening, and communication.
notes: Not open to students with credit in MUSIC 151

title: Beginner Class Piano for Non-Music Majors
description: Beginner Class Piano is designed for non-music majors with little or no experience to develop basic piano technique, explore appropriate-level piano literature, and study rudimentary elements of music including rhythm, melody, harmony, and improvisation.
notes: Not open to music majors.

title: Piano - Elementary Class Instruction
description: Basic keyboard experience through study of music reading, notation, scales, chords, and sight-reading covering a repertoire of beginning and intermediate songs and piano literature, with emphasis on keyboard harmony. description: Survey of Western art music from the Middle Ages to the Enlightenment, examining genres, styles, and practices within their historical, cultural, sociopolitical, technological, and aesthetic contexts. Emphasis on music historiography and the interpretation of primary sources.

title: Music History II: American Revolution to the Present
description: Survey of Western art music from the American Revolution to the present, examining genres, styles, and practices within their historical, cultural, sociopolitical, technological, and aesthetic contexts. Emphasis on music historiography and the interpretation of primary sources.
notes: Not open to students who have completed MUSIC 308B and MUSIC 308DW

title: Music Literature for Children
description: Analytical study of music suitable for children of all ages. Background information, musical structure and functions of this music in the lives of children.

title: Music Cultures of the World
description: Art, folk, popular, and sacred music case studies drawn from Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, and the United States with attention to the relationship between culture, history, and music. Concert attendance required in Fall and Spring semesters.

title: Practicum in Music Education III
description: Practical teaching applications. Students will develop and teach model lessons evaluated by students, faculty, and master teachers. Students choose a primary area of specialization and a master teacher in preparation for the final semester of the practicum series.

title: Conducting

title: Conducting II
description: Elements of baton technique and development of skills common to instrumental conducting. Representative literature and techniques for instrumental organizations studied and performed. Practical experience in typical conducting situations.

title: Research and Writing for Musicians
description: Capstone seminar for music majors emphasizing advanced research and professional writing. Students navigate information resources, critically evaluate music, performances, and scholarship, and produce a formal research paper and presentation on an original topic. Fulfills the university’s Graduate Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR).
notes: Not open to students with credit in MUSIC 308DW and MUSIC 408DW. Satisfies the Graduation Writing Assessment Requirement (GWAR) for students who get a minimum grade of C or Cr. Upper-division courses should only be taken by students who have completed 60 semester units or more. In exceptional cases, a student who has completed fewer than 60 units may enroll in upper division courses.

title: Practicum in Music Education IV
